territorial_scope.description: Applies within South Dakota; section 5 gives legal effect in state law to convictions in other states for second-offense purposes.

evidence.quote: Any conviction for, or plea of guilty to, an offense in another state that, if committed in this state, would be a violation of sections 2 to 4, inclusive, of this Act

summary.short: Revises South Dakota child pornography offenses: creates felony crimes of possessing, distributing and manufacturing child pornography, including computer-generated depictions made with artificial intelligence, with mandatory minimum prison terms for first and repeat offenses; also amends related sex-offense, sentencing and juvenile sexting provisions. The text states no effective date.
summary.long: Amends South Dakota's child pornography statutes. Section 1 revises definitions in § 22-24A-2, adding 'computer-generated child pornography', which includes an individual indistinguishable from an actual minor created by artificial intelligence or other computer technology, and a 'child-like sex doll' definition. Sections 2 to 4 create offenses of possessing (Class 4 felony), distributing (Class 3) and manufacturing (Class 2) child pornography, each with mandatory minimum prison terms for first and subsequent offenses. Section 5 counts out-of-state convictions toward second-offense status. Section 6 requires a § 22-22-1.3 assessment after conviction. Section 7 makes minor consent and mistake of age no defense. Section 8 gives an affirmative defense where the depiction is of the accused alone. Section 9 allows a departure from mandatory sentences on written findings of mitigating circumstances. Related amendments cover sentencing (§ 22-6-11), indecent exposure (§ 22-24-1.2; a prior felony conviction under sections 2 to 4 makes it a Class 6 felony), a nudity exemption (§ 22-24A-20), the sex-crime list (§ 22-24B-1) and juvenile sexting (§ 26-10-33; a Class 1 misdemeanor for minors). Section 15 repeals § 22-24A-3.

notes: Session act; the bill number and effective date do not appear in the text (registry title only). Amended provisions are printed in full without markings, so new text cannot be separated from restated text; annotated as amendments per the section headings. Target instrument ids are empty because the codified SDCL sections are not in the registry. Section 1 defines 'Simulated' by reference to subdivision (16) (bestiality), not (17) (prohibited sexual act), while sections 2 to 4 use 'simulation of a prohibited sexual act'; possible cross-reference error. Section 14 refers to 22-24A-2(10) and (17). No named firms or facilities; the Department of Corrections (Section 10) is mentioned only as a supervising body, with no duty assigned.

evidence.quote: A conviction under this section for a second or subsequent offense
"Adult," any person eighteen years of age or older;
"Child pornography," any image or visual depiction of a minor engaged in prohibited sexual acts;
"Child" or "minor," any person under the age of eighteen years;
The term also includes any on-line service, internet service, or internet bulletin board;
"Computer-generated child pornography," any visual depiction of:

"Digital media," any electronic storage device, including a floppy disk or other magnetic storage device or any compact disc that has memory and the capacity to store audio, video, or written materials;
"Indistinguishable," when used with respect to a visual depiction, means virtually indistinguishable;
"Nudity," the showing or the simulated showing of the human male or female genitals, pubic area, or buttocks with less than a fully opaque covering;

"Person," includes individuals, children, firms, associations, joint ventures, partnerships, estates, trusts, business trusts, syndicates, fiduciaries, corporations, and all other groups or combinations;
"Prohibited sexual act," actual or simulated sexual intercourse, sadism, masochism, sexual bestiality, incest, masturbation, or sadomasochistic abuse;

"Visual depiction," any developed and undeveloped film, photograph, slide and videotape, and any photocopy, drawing, printed or written material, and any data stored on computer disk, digital media, or by electronic means that are capable of conversion into a visual image.
